npcs.name: Oona
npcs.title: a soul who finished — done, at peace, and ready to go
npcs.hail: *(An old woman sits on a plain bench at the road's edge, hands folded, watching the grey with an expression you have not once seen in all your walking of the dead lands: contentment. Not resignation, not the brittle calm of the resigned — contentment, whole and unhurried, the ease of someone who has set down everything they were carrying and found they can sit up straight without it. She is faded at the edges, going soon, and she does not seem to mind. She watches you approach, and her face does something that stops you: it fills with a gentle, particular concern — for you.)* …*(softly)* …oh, *child.* …*(she says it though you are no child, and are cold, and are the one soul the Wall gave back, and it does not matter)* …*come* and *sit.* …*(she pats the bench)* …*no* — not because *i* need the *company.* i'm *quite* alright, i'm — i'm about *done*, truth be told, and *glad* of it. …*(her eyes are kind and clear and they see you)* …*you* look like you *need* to *sit* down …a great deal *more* …than *i* need someone to *sit* with. …when did you last *let* someone *look* at *you*, cold one? …*properly?* …*(she waits, unhurried)* …*i've* the *time.* …in fact …the *time* is *all* i've *got* *left* …and i'd *like* …to *spend* it …on *you.*

variants.text: *(Her clear old eyes travel over you and her contentment does not dim but sharpens toward you, the way a lamp turns toward a cold room.)* …*(gently, and it lands like a hand on a fever)* …oh, you're *further* down the *cold* road than you *know*, aren't you. …i can *see* it. the *frost* halfway up your *arms*, the *feeling* going *quiet* in you, the *names* you've *kept* starting to *weigh* on you like *stones* instead of *warming* you like *coals.* …*(she pats the bench, unhurried, certain)* …*sit.* …you've spent — how *long*, cold one? — going from *soul* to *soul*, carrying *everyone's* *grief* and *setting* down *none* of your *own.* …*being* the *warm* thing for *everyone* …while the *cold* *climbs* *you.* …*(softly)* …*nobody's* *sat* you *down.* …i can *tell.* …well. …*i've* nothing *left* to *do* but *finish*, and *finishing* can *wait* an *hour.* …*let* an *old* woman …*sit* you *down.*

*(She marks the bare place where no god sits on you, and instead of the wariness or the pity you have learned to expect, she only smiles, warm and unbothered.)* …*no* *god* on you. …*(she nods, as if this confirms something kind)* …*neither* on *me*, child. never *was.* …and here i *sit*, *finished* and *content* and *ready*, *Unclaimed* as the *day* i *died*, and i'll tell you a *secret* the *Wall* would *rather* you *never* *learned:* …a *soul* doesn't *need* a *god* to *finish* *well.* …i tended a *garden* and *loved* a *few* *people* *badly* and *well* and *raised* what i *could* and *said* my *sorrys* and my *thank*-*yous* …and *no* *god* *claimed* me and it *did* *not* *matter*, because *i* *claimed* *myself.* …*(she pats the bench)* …*come.* *sit* with the *proof.* …the *Unclaimed* can *finish* *whole.* …*i* did. …and *you* — *(her eyes soften)* …*you* can *too*, cold one. …but *not* if you *never* *stop* *walking.*

*(She watches you with that unhurried, seeing warmth, and pats the bench again, patient as the grey is patient, but kinder.)* …*sit*, i *said.* …*(a small smile)* …you're *braced* for me to *ask* you *something.* they *all* are, when i *wave* them *over* — *everyone* in the *dead* lands *wants* *something*, and *you* most of *all*, i'd *wager*, being the *one* they *all* *come* to. …*(she shakes her head)* …i *don't* want *anything*, child. i'm *done.* *finished.* *ready.* …the *only* thing i've *got* left to *give* …is an *hour* of *someone* *looking* at *you* …instead of *you* *looking* at *them.* …*(she waits)* …*sit* *down*, cold one. …*let* it be *your* *turn.*

nodes.speaker: Oona
nodes.text: *(She makes room on the bench though there is room enough, and folds her hands, and looks at you the way no one has looked at you since you came back from the dead — as a soul to be tended, not a service to be used.)* …*here's* how it *is* with me, so you'll *believe* i've *nothing* to *ask.* …i *lived* a *long* while, and a *plain* one. i *buried* a *husband* and *made* my *peace* with it. i *hurt* my *daughter* *once*, *badly*, and i *lived* to *mend* it, and we *mended* it, and she *held* my *hand* at the *end.* …i *said* every *sorry* i *owed.* i *heard* every *thank*-*you* i *needed.* …*(she spreads her faded hands, serene)* …i came *here* with *nothing* *unfinished*, cold one — which is the *rarest* thing in the *grey*, i've come to *learn* — and so i've just been …*sitting.* *content.* *waiting* to *dissolve*, which doesn't *frighten* me, because a *thing* that's *finished* …doesn't *fear* the *ending.* …*(she turns her clear eyes on you)* …*that's* my *whole* *tale.* …*now.* …*(gently)* …*yours.* …when did *you* last let *anyone* *ask?*

choices.text: *(read the one soul in the grey who's genuinely at peace — not to help her, just to understand a thing you've never seen)* "Let me look at you a moment, Oona. Not to fix anything. I just — I've never seen a finished soul before. I want to understand what it looks like."
*(the reflex — try to help her, the way you help everyone)* "Is there nothing you need, Oona? Truly? Something carried, someone found, a word sent? Let me do something for you before you go."

*(the one the Wall gave back — and what it's cost)* "You should know what you're offering to sit with, Oona. I'm the soul the Wall let out. I walk in and out of the dark everyone else only walks into. And the cost of it — the thing no one sees, because they only ever need me — is that I carry a little of every soul's grief out with me, and none of it ever thaws, and I think I'm going cold. Slowly. You're the first one to look at that instead of past it."

*(let it be your turn — sit down, and let her)* "...Alright, Oona. Alright. I'll sit. Look at me, then. It's been — I can't remember the last time it was my turn. Do the thing you're offering. I'm too tired to pretend I don't need it."
"How, Oona? How do you finish? I've watched a hundred souls fail to, and one manage it, and I don't understand the difference."
"I can't stay, Oona. There are others who need — there's always someone who needs. Thank you, though. For offering."

nodes.speaker: Oona
nodes.text: *(She lets you look, amused and willing, and your sense — so practiced at finding the wound, the ache, the unfinished thing — reaches into her and finds, for the first time in all your walking, none of it.)* *(And it is genuinely strange to witness. There is no snag, no held breath, no grief papered over, no self spent or hidden or hoarded. Your sense reads a soul that used itself all the way up in the living of a life — spent its love, made its amends, took its joys, wept its losses, and arrived at the end with the accounts genuinely settled — and so there is nothing here for the grey to grind on, nothing for the Wall to catch, nothing to keep her. She is not brave about dissolving. She is not resigned to it. She is *finished*, the way a good day is finished when the light goes, without grievance, having been fully lived. And your sense reads the thing that turns your own chest cold to find, because it is aimed at you: that in the whole serene expanse of her there is exactly one active want left, one last small fire she has kept lit past all the others, and it is not for herself. It is for *you.* She has looked at the cold soul who came up the road carrying everyone's grief and none of its own comfort, and she has decided — freely, gladly, with the only hour she has left — that she would rather spend her ending *tending the one who tends everyone* than dissolve a moment sooner in peace. And your sense reads, under that, the thing she knows about you that you have been refusing to know about yourself: that you are further down the cold road than any of the souls you've been saving, and that no one — not one, in all your crossing — has ever once sat *you* down.)*

nodes.speaker: Oona
nodes.text: *(She laughs, softly, delighted and not at all surprised.)* …*there* it is. …*(she shakes her head, fond)* …i *knew* you'd try. the one who *carries* *everyone* can't *sit* for a *breath* without *reaching* for someone *else's* *load.* …*(gently, firmly)* …*no*, child. there's *nothing* to *carry.* *nothing* to *find.* *nobody* to *send* a *word* to — my *daughter* *held* my *hand* at the *end* and we said *everything*, there's not a *syllable* *left* *owing* in *either* *direction.* …*(she reaches over and, astonishingly, takes your cold hand in her faded warm one)* …you *cannot* *help* me, cold one, because i am the *one* soul in this *whole* *grey* *country* who *doesn't* *need* it. …*(she holds your hand, and does not let go)* …which is *exactly* …*why* i'm the *one* who can *finally* *help* *you.* …*a* *soul* with *nothing* *left* to *want* for *itself* …is the *only* *safe* *place* …a *soul* like *you* …can *set* *something* *down.* …*(she pats your hand)* …so *stop* *reaching.* …and *tell* me. …what's the *heaviest* *thing* you're *carrying* …that you've *never* *once* …*put* *down?*

nodes.speaker: Oona
nodes.text: *(She listens — really listens, the whole of her turned toward you — and when you finish, she does not flinch from the cold in you the way the living flinched, the way even the dead flinch. She nods, slow and grave and kind.)* …*going* *cold.* …*(she says it back to you gently, making it real by naming it, the way you have named a hundred souls' truths and never once had your own named back)* …*yes.* …i *can* *see* it. i've *watched* it *creep* up you the *whole* time you've been *standing* there *bracing* to be *useful.* …*(she tightens her hold on your hand)* …*here* is what *no* one has *told* you, child, because they *need* you too *badly* to *want* it *true:* …the *cold* isn't the *Wall* taking you. …the *cold* is what happens to a soul that *pours* *out* *warmth* *forever* …and *never* *once* *lets* any *back* *in.* …*(her eyes are wet and steady)* …you are not *fading*, cold one. you are *starving.* …you've fed the *whole* *grey* …and *forgotten* that a *fire* *needs* *feeding* *too.* …*(she draws you down toward the bench)* …*sit.* …*let* the *one* soul who *wants* *nothing* *from* you …*put* a *little* *warmth* *back.* …it's the *only* thing …that *stops* the *cold*, child. …not *mercy* *given.* …*mercy* *taken.* …*(barely)* …*when* did you *last* …*take* *any?*

nodes.speaker: Oona
nodes.text: *(You sit. It is the first time you have sat since you came back — really sat, not perched to listen, not knelt to read a soul, but *sat*, with your weight down and your guard lowered, beside someone who wants nothing from you. And Oona looks at you, and does for you the thing you have done for a hundred souls and never once had done for you: she sees you.)* …*there.* …*(she settles your cold hand between her two faded warm ones and holds it like something worth holding)* …*look* at you. …the one who *crosses.* the one they *all* *reach* for. …*carrying* — gods, child, i can *feel* it — the *mother* in the *Wall*, and the *child* at the *step*, and the *storyteller* coming *apart*, and *every* *verdict* you *handed* *down* that you're *not* *sure* of, and the *cold* of *all* of them *stacked* in you like *winters.* …*(she strokes the back of your hand)* …and *nobody* — *nobody* — has *ever* *said* the *simple* thing to *you.* …so *hear* it, from a *soul* with *nothing* to *gain* by *saying* it: …*you* *are* *doing* *enough.* …*you* *are* *allowed* to be *tired.* …the *griefs* you *carry* are *not* *yours* to *keep* *warm* *forever* — you can *set* them by the *fire* and *let* them *cool*, and it does *not* *make* you *cruel*, it makes you a *soul* instead of a *service.* …*(her voice is very soft now, and going, and glad)* …and *when* you *fade*, cold one — *whenever* that *is* — you will *not* fade *unwitnessed.* …because *right* *now*, on this *bench*, at the *end* of my *road* …*i* *saw* you. …*whole.* …*tired.* …*good.* …and *worth* *sitting* *down.* …*(she is dissolving now, gently, content, her last hour spent exactly as she chose)* …*don't* *thank* me. …just — *(fading)* …just *let* it *have* *happened.* …*let* *one* *soul* …have *tended* *you* …and *don't* *walk* it *off.* …*carry* *this* one *warm* thing …the way you *carry* all the *cold* ones. …*(and she is gone, into the ending she was ready for, and where she sat there is a warmth on the bench, and it does not fade for a long, long while.)*

nodes.speaker: Oona
nodes.text: *(She considers the question with the seriousness it deserves, an old woman who has clearly turned it over herself.)* …*how* to *finish.* …*(she nods)* …i've *watched* the *ones* who *can't*, same as you. and the *difference* isn't *goodness*, cold one — some of the *kindest* souls i *knew* couldn't *finish*, and some *right* *bastards* went *easy.* …*(she folds her hands)* …the *difference* is *this:* the *ones* who *can't* *finish* are the *ones* who *left* something *unsaid.* a *sorry* they *swallowed.* a *love* they *never* *spoke.* a *grudge* they *fed* instead of *setting* *down.* an *account* left *open.* …and the *grey* *catches* on the *open* *account* like *wool* on a *nail*, and *holds* them, and they *fray.* …*(she looks at you, and the point of it arrives)* …*i* *finished* because i *closed* my *accounts* while i *still* *could.* i *said* the *sorry.* i *spoke* the *love.* i *put* the *grudge* *down.* …*(gently, pointedly)* …*you*, cold one, are *walking* the *grey* with *how* *many* *accounts* *open?* …*how* many *sorrys* *swallowed?* how many *times* have you *needed* *tending* …and *swallowed* *that*, and *walked* *on?* …*(she pats the bench)* …*finish* *well* means *close* your *accounts.* …and the *first* one *you* owe …*(softly)* …is to *yourself.* …*sit.* …*start* *there.*

nodes.speaker: Oona
nodes.text: *(She nods, unsurprised and unhurt, and folds her hands back into her contented lap.)* …*of* *course* there is. …there's *always* someone who *needs.* …*(she smiles, and there is no reproach in it, only a knowing so gentle it is almost worse than reproach)* …*go* *on*, then, cold one. *go* and be the *warm* thing for the *next* one, and the *next.* …*(and as you turn, softly, without weight)* …but *hear* an *old* woman, who's *finishing* and has *nothing* to *gain* by *lying* to you: …the *day* will *come* when *you* need to *finish* *too.* when the *cold's* *all* the *way* up. and on *that* *day* …you'll *wish* you'd *learned* — *here*, *now*, from *me* — *how* to *let* a *soul* *sit* you *down.* …*(she settles back)* …*come* *back* …if the *road* *ever* *lets* you. …the *bench* …*holds* *two.* …*it* *always* *did.*
